description: Part 2, Limits on the number of grades (G-08, Deeper). The six-site family optima at tau = .20 (exactly G and the fixed orders) are six.A.eq*.tau20.* and six.A.order*.tau20.* in part2.json, and the theory book's fixed-order risks tb14.four.tau25.eq4.risk and tb14.four.tau25.le4.risk too; this fragment adds what the G-08 page writes about the theory book's four-unit law (ch. 14, sec-fixed-order-dp-example: two states with probabilities 3/4 and 1/4, two criteria weighted 3/5 and 2/5, tau = 1/4): its state probabilities, the weighted pair error of B above C, the best reports of the four families the widget shows at tau = 1/4 and their sizes.

g08.tb14.note: theory book ch. 14: state 1 (3/4) orders ABCD on criterion 1 and ACBD on criterion 2, state 2 (1/4) BACD and DCBA; values 4, 3, 2, 1 along each order (the same law as tb16.four in part2.json)

g08.tb14.probs.note: the two state probabilities gathered as a one-state law (means = the values)

g08.tb14.tau25.eq4.note: exactly 4 grades among all reports (the 24 strict orders)

g08.tb14.tau25.order.note: every contiguous cut of A, B, C, D (8 reports), the theory book's setting

g08.tb14.ebar.BC.note: the weighted error of B above C (theory book table: 2/5)

g08.tb14.ebar.AB.note: the weighted error of A above B (theory book table: 1/4, equal to tau)

g08.tb14.e2.BC.note: criterion 2 error of B above C: 1 (B is below C on criterion 2 in both states)

g08.tb14.tau25.eq4.risk.note: 7/40, the same as the fixed-order value tb14.four.tau25.eq4.risk

g08.tb14.tau25.all.risk.note: 3/20, the same as the fixed-order value tb14.four.tau25.le4.risk
